answer: Each clear night the observatory takes bearings from the pole star and seals the chart, and only a sealed chart may guide a party across the ice. A shale bearing copied from an old almanac fails the sky: at the garden of the night the pole star must stand where the chart claims, and a copied bearing walks the party into open water. Forging the charts means observing for two winters, taking 380 bearings and paying 17,200, while the forge seal on the chart is checked by the station chief before every departure, so a bearing that was never taken is burned.
